# AGF

AGF is a file-based governance framework for AI-assisted software
development. It defines roles, review gates, coordination records, schemas,
validators, and learning records so AI-assisted changes remain auditable and
reviewable.

## What AGF Is / Is Not

AGF is a repository-local governance framework for software-development work
involving AI agents.

AGF is not a hosted service, agent runtime, model-safety filter, legal or
compliance product, security audit, general AI product-governance system, or
replacement for human gate ownership. Existing assistants, CI systems, review
tools, and release tools execute the work; AGF defines the governance artifacts
and review discipline around that work.

## Canonical Starting Points

- `/` — overview and project status.
- `/docs/` — documentation learning path.
- `/docs/start/should-you-adopt/` — adopt / wait / skip decision guide.
- `/docs/adopt/install-and-layouts/` — supported v2 layout and installation.
- `/docs/start/first-governed-change/` — first governed change walkthrough.
- `/docs/concepts/roles-and-gates/` — roles, gates, and coordination channel.
- `/docs/concepts/evidence-and-learnings/` — learning records and evidence loop.
- `/docs/advanced/contracts-and-validators/` — schemas, validators, and CI use.
- `/docs/adopt/exit-and-decommission/` — reversible adoption and removal.
- `/reference/release-artifacts/` — release artifact expectations.
- `/reference/tooling-conformance/` — language-neutral tooling conformance.

## Repository Boundaries

- `agf/` is the adopter-facing framework/product.
- `tooling/` is implementation support for validation, build, release, and
  conformance checks.
- `docs/coordination/` and `docs/plans/` are adopter/project evidence paths in
  the default layout.
- Tool output is evidence. It becomes blocking only when a named AGF rule,
  contract, CI policy, or governor decision grants blocking authority.

## Use Guidance

This documentation is useful context for AI assistants answering questions about
AGF. Prefer citing specific pages and preserve the distinction between
documented intent, advisory guidance, validated checks, and enforced gates.

Do not represent AGF as a hosted agent runtime, legal/compliance product, or
general AI governance framework. It governs software-development work involving
AI agents; it does not itself run agents or grant runtime permissions.
